No day-level deadline is published on the Foundation's programme page.

official.tuition_coverage_note: The Foundation states it supports the full tuition fee for 4 semesters for master's students and for 6 semesters for doctoral and integrated master's and doctoral course students.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-tuition-plus-living Korean graduate scholarship from the POSCO TJ Park Foundation for non-Korean nationals, with KRW 1,000,000 a month for living expenses, a one-off KRW 1,000,000 settlement payment, National Health Insurance covered, and Korean language education thrown in - and only 20 students a year get it. The decisive detail is that you do not apply to the Foundation: you must be admitted to a master's or doctoral programme at a Foundation-affiliated graduate school in Korea and then be recommended by that university, so your real target is the November graduate admissions round, not the Foundation. The cycle then runs through December recommendations, January interviews and a February announcement.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Korean nationals, including dual nationals whose second nationality is not Korean, seeking a master's or doctoral degree at a Foundation-affiliated Korean graduate school
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold non-Korean nationality and are not a dual national holding Korean citizenship, which is an absolute bar
Identify graduate schools in Korea affiliated with the Foundation and check their November graduate admissions round rather than any Foundation deadline
Aim for master's, doctoral or integrated master's and doctoral admission, since these are the only supported levels
Understand that the university then recommends you to the Foundation in December under its own standards, so your priority is being a strong institutional candidate
Prepare for a Foundation interview around January and expect the announcement around February with an award ceremony in March
Budget around 22 months of living expenses at master's level and 36 at doctoral or integrated level, matched to 4 and 6 semesters of tuition respectively
common_rejection_risks: Holding Korean dual citizenship, which makes you ineligible outright
Trying to apply directly to the Foundation rather than going through an affiliated graduate school's recommendation
Targeting a graduate school that is not affiliated with the Foundation, which removes you from the route entirely
Assuming a self-funded or language-institute pathway will count, since the support is tied to master's, doctoral or integrated programme admission
Expecting more than 20 awards a year; the Foundation states the figure is subject to change and competition is intense
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Airfare to and from Korea, since the Foundation lists an initial settlement fee and health insurance but no travel benefit, and any living costs beyond KRW 1,000,000 per month
document_audit: The Foundation publishes no application document list, because the document chain runs through the university - so prepare for those requirements instead
Your nationality status needs to be evidenced to the university, since dual Korean citizens are excluded from the award
alerts: The Foundation's schedule is by month, not by date: watch the November admissions round, not a Foundation deadline
The award count of 20 per year is expressly subject to change, so do not plan on a fixed cohort size
Tuition support and living expense support run on different clocks - 4 or 6 semesters for tuition against 22 or 36 months for living expenses - so plan your graduation timeline against both
Benefits include non-cash support such as Korean language education, welfare services and cultural experience programs, so the value of the award exceeds the cash figures
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure master's or doctoral admission at a Foundation-affiliated Korean graduate school in the November round, let the university recommend you to the Foundation in December, then attend the January interview and await the February announcement

official.status_note: The National Institute for International Education's page for the Global Korea Scholarship Non-degree Exchange Program is live, states the programme supports selected international exchange students at affiliated universities in Korea, and directs applicants to their university's own exchange office for the timing.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a one-semester exchange grant worth KRW 630,000 a month plus round-trip economy airfare, with accommodation, settlement and insurance costs handled - which makes Korea a genuinely affordable semester abroad, but you must first be on your home university's exchange programme with a Korean institution. Selection works in three stages: your home university picks its applicants, the intended Korean university recommends them, and the National Institute for International Education makes the final call. You need an above-80% GPA, and if you are going only to study Korean language courses this programme will not support you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Third- or fourth-year undergraduates and graduate students at overseas universities with exchange agreements with Korean universities, with strong grades of above 80%
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the Korean side of your exchange is at a university affiliated with the National Institute for International Education, which is the gating condition
Check your GPA is above 80% or the equivalent, since that is a stated eligibility threshold
Confirm you are enrolled in a degree exchange programme, because those enrolled only in Korean language courses are excluded
Contact your home university's exchange office early, since they build the applicant pool and the university-level deadline governs the timing
Confirm you are not a former beneficiary of a Korean government scholarship and do not hold Korean citizenship, both of which are bars
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the National Institute for International Education directly instead of through your university's exchange office
Being enrolled in a Korean-language-only course track, which is explicitly not supported
Targeting a Korean university that is not affiliated with the programme
Having previously received a scholarship from the Korean government, or holding Korean citizenship including dual nationality
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition, which the National Institute for International Education does not list as covered, plus any spending beyond the monthly allowance and the economy-class airfare reimbursement
document_audit: The National Institute for International Education publishes no document checklist, because the document chain runs through your university - so satisfy your own university's exchange-office requirements fully and on time
Keep evidence of your exchange placement with the affiliated Korean university, since that is what the recommendation route depends on
alerts: Deadlines vary by university, so the date that matters is your own university's exchange-office cut-off, not anything on the national site
Your academic result at the home university, not at the Korean host, is what is assessed for eligibility
The airfare is reimbursed based on the actual cost of the most economical airfare, so book economy rather than expecting a premium ticket
Study loss of credit and results after arrival must be reported to your home university, not to the National Institute for International Education
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through your home university's exchange office for a placement at a Korean university affiliated with the National Institute for International Education, be recommended by that university, and let the National Institute for International Education make the final selection
